description: We are ÉCLIPSE, a team of developers, designers, and space enthusiasts collaborating for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to build an immersive space mission game. Just as an eclipse is a rare and awe-inspiring alignment of celestial bodies, our team brings together the worlds of astronomy, data science, and gaming to create something extraordinary
summary:
Artemis IV: Gateway to the Moon is a browser-based, interactive aerospace simulation developed by Team Éclipse for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Built with HTML5 Canvas 2D, Three.js WebGL, and the Web Audio API, it lets anyone experience the pivotal fourth mission of NASA’s Artemis program with zero installation required.

Players command every critical flight phase: launching the super-heavy SLS Block 1B rocket through Max-Q and stage separation, plotting a 3D gravitational slingshot to deliver the international I-Hab module to the Lunar Gateway in Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit, piloting the Human Landing System down to Shackleton Crater at the lunar South Pole, and threading Earth’s narrow 2.0° atmospheric corridor for a 25,000 mph skip-entry return. To mirror real mission stakes, Orion’s propellant reserve carries over across phases, forcing players to balance orbital maneuvers against fuel needed to come home.

By pairing hands-on Newtonian physics with live telemetry, an offline CAPCOM AI flight controller, and an unlockable engineering archive, the project transforms complex orbital mechanics and deep-space exploration into an intuitive, accessible educational tool that inspires the next generation of explorers.
details:
Artemis IV: Gateway to the Moon is an interactive, browser-based educational game designed by Team Éclipse to introduce kids and young learners to the real science behind NASA’s return to the Moon. Built with HTML5 Canvas 2D, Three.js WebGL, and the Web Audio API, it runs instantly in any web browser with zero downloads or setup.

Instead of reading dense textbooks, kids step into the commander's seat across four hands-on space missions: launching the mega-rocket SLS Block 1B, slinging past Earth in 3D to dock with the Lunar Gateway, landing on the Moon’s South Pole in low gravity, and piloting Orion safely home through a fiery skip-reentry. Along the way, an interactive CAPCOM AI buddy answers space questions, live "Real NASA Science" popups explain physics as it happens, and beating the mission unlocks an illustrated comic finale and visual NASA space archive.
